label: ex:chi-minus-six-derivation
title: $\chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6$: the derivation chain
html:
We present the chain that fixes \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6, the Euler characteristic of the base curve (the three Euler characteristics). Steps 1--4 and 6--7 run forward from the QOU triple. Step 5, which fixes the branch-point count at six, reads that count off the Weierstrass points of Bring's surface — the surface the chain then identifies at Step 7 — so the chain locates the value rather than deriving it from the axioms alone. Step 8 applies the motivic perpetual obstruction theorem (proved via Route A: prime-ideal collapse, C = a_0(-1) + 2 \cdot a_1(-1)).

Step 1: Start with the QOU triple. We have (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) with gauge group G = \mathrm{SU}(2). The chain tracks the fundamental object V — the two-dimensional simple object of the volume axiom — which is distinct from the Frobenius–Hopf object A; \tau is the fibre functor.

Step 2: The fibre functor produces a rank-2 bundle. The fibre functor \tau maps V to a rank-2 vector bundle, still written V, over a compact Riemann surface M_0. Since G = \mathrm{SU}(2), the determinant \det(V) is trivial. Thus \deg(V) = 0.

Step 3: Apply Riemann--Roch. For a rank-r bundle of degree d over a genus-g surface:

  \chi(M_0, V) = d + r(1 - g) = 0 + 2(1 - g) = 2 - 2g

Step 4: Obstructions require g \geq 1. The lifting obstructions require \kappa_n \neq 0 at every level of the brane tower. The obstruction classes lie in H^2(M_0, B). For these to be non-trivial, we need H^2(M_0, \mathbb{C}^*) \neq 0, which requires g \geq 1.

Step 5: The Frobenius--Hopf structure fixes 6 branch points. The Frobenius--Hopf structure forces the algebra to have exactly 6 branch points in its geometric descent (from the six Weierstrass points fixed by each transposition in S_5 -- Bring's curve carries 60 in a single \mathrm{Aut}-orbit and 60 = 6 \times 10 -- whose degree-2 quotient has genus 1). This fixes |\chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0)| = 6.

Step 6: The sign is negative. The bundle has more obstructions than sections. Specifically, \chi(M_0, V) = -6 means h^0(V) - h^1(V) = -6, so h^1(V) \geq 6 (obstructions dominate).

Step 7: Therefore g = 4. From \chi(M_0, V) = 2 - 2g = -6, we obtain g = 4. (The sheaf Euler characteristic \chi(M_0, V) coincides with the topological \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g only because \mathrm{rk}\, V = 2 and \deg V = 0; see the three Euler characteristics.) The unique maximally symmetric genus-4 curve is Bring's surface \Sigma_4, with automorphism group S_5 of order 120.

Step 8 (motivic-Galois reading). Steps 4 and 5 lift to a single algebraic statement at the level of the motivic substrate. The condition \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 controls the value of the substrate's motivic L-function at the boundary of analytic continuation. The non-vanishing of the obstruction classes \kappa_n at every level becomes the non-vanishing of the Frobenius character at every finite place p \nmid 6. This is the content of the motivic perpetual obstruction theorem applied with \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 (Kummer tower §motivic-Galois). The "g \geq 1" condition (Step 4) is the cyclotomic-place criterion H^1_{\mathrm{Gal}}(\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p), \mu_n(1)) \neq 0, realised at every p. The Riemann–Roch derivation is the archimedean shadow (v = \infty realization) of this stronger adelic statement.
